original_test_intent: Verify the specific USB management path from the BMC to the USB hub associated with the CX9 device in Bay B, including correct bay isolation and the complete required downstream functions, not merely the presence of any platform USB hub.
original_method: Prove Bay B chassis position and CX9 serial/PN/slot identity, map the BMC USB controller/root port across the HPM/PCI-board connector chain to the Bay B CX9 hub, define the authoritative enumeration endpoint, exact hub port/VID:PID/product/serial/speed and per-port CX9 children; have an operator inspect/photograph the Bay B route; capture full unfiltered topology/descriptors and reset/error logs; compare against a Bay-B-specific oracle and leave USB/CX9 state unchanged.
manual_activity: An operator verifies the physical Bay B location and CX9 identity, photographs the BMC/HPM/PCI-board-to-Bay-B-CX9 cable and connectors, and leaves the management link undisturbed during read-only collection.
required_inputs: Bay B position and CX9 serial/PN/slot identity with Bay A distinction
BMC controller/root-port through HPM/PCI-board connector chain to Bay B CX9 hub and enumeration-owner map
Hub plus per-port CX9 downstream VID:PID/product/serial/class/speed manifest
Hub-only versus all-downstream acceptance decision, error limits, physical procedure and recovery
safety_requirements: Bind topology to Bay B and the intended CX9; explicitly exclude Bay A and other identical hubs
Use read-only complete tree/descriptors and preserve CX9/BMC/USB health logs
Do not unplug/replug, reset, deauthorize, unbind/rebind, update or power-cycle the CX9 or management hub
Do not clear kernel/BMC evidence or retry a flapping link automatically
Stop on wrong-bay identity, CX9 management loss, USB reset storm, speed downgrade or device movement; no automatic retry
agent_execution_scope: Validate Bay B/CX9 identity, physical/logical BMC path, enumeration endpoint and frozen hub/child oracle
After operator physical confirmation, capture full USB topology/descriptors plus CX9/BMC/USB health/error evidence
Compare every Bay-B-specific port, child identity and speed and document missing, unexpected, cross-bay or moved devices
Do not accept a generic/Bay A hub, use insecure/truncated collection, alter CX9/USB state or issue the DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Resolve whether the Criteria requires only the exact Bay B CX9 hub or also all downstream devices from the Procedure
Approve Bay B/CX9 identity, complete BMC-HPM-PCI route, enumeration surface and per-port device/speed manifest
Review bay-bound physical/topology/stability evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: `lsusb` can support the read-only portion only when the collection endpoint is mapped to the BMC-to-Bay-B route. `grep/head` removes topology and completeness; `sshpass` plus host-key bypass is unsafe.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Capture authenticated complete `lsusb -t`, full hub/child descriptors and USB/CX9 error history on the authoritative endpoint, correlated to the operator-confirmed Bay B CX9 identity and cable route.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: BMC-to-Bay B CX9 USB hub scope, AI_VR_USB_BMC_to_CX9 bundle and 30/30-minute allocation remain; bay, hub and child identities are not inferred.

modernized_recommendation.status: LOW READ-ONLY BAY-B-CX9-BOUND USB HUB AND DOWNSTREAM CHECK
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use chassis/bay and CX9 serial identity to anchor the physical route, then validate the exact USB port tree and all approved CX9 downstream functions against a Bay-B-specific manifest.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds cross-bay exclusion, CX9 identity, connector-chain provenance, per-child speeds and complete stability evidence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Identical hubs in multiple bays make generic `lsusb` output especially prone to false attribution; hub presence also cannot prove all CX9 management functions enumerate.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: The USB path may carry CX9 management or firmware interfaces, so resets/rebinds can disrupt device manageability even if dataplane PCIe remains present.

project_override_considerations: If Bay B is intentionally unpopulated, use an approved population/N-A rule; do not substitute Bay A. A host view is acceptable only with documented mapping to the BMC-rooted CX9 management path.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash, authorization, acceptance decision and Bay B/CX9 serial/PN/slot proof
Complete authoritative USB tree and descriptors for exact hub and every expected CX9 child with speeds
Bay-B-specific oracle comparison including missing, unexpected, cross-bay, moved or downgraded devices
Pre/post USB/CX9/BMC reset/error/health evidence and stable management state
Conflict disposition, discrepancy/recovery record and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure requires all Bay B CX9 downstream devices to be shown, while Criteria marks hub detection alone as PASS. An empty or partial CX9 management tree could satisfy the latter.

review_improvement: Adds Bay B/CX9 identity and cross-bay exclusion while preserving the acceptance conflict, preventing a generic or Bay A hub from satisfying this specific management-path testcase.
independent_technical_reasoning: The Bay B qualifier is the distinguishing coverage. Multi-bay systems can expose nearly identical USB hubs, so port path alone may still need CX9 serial/slot correlation. The Procedure's downstream requirement matters because the hub IC can enumerate while CX9 child functions do not. Therefore evidence must be Bay-specific and child-complete, and the hub-only Criteria must remain an explicit conflict for the engineer rather than silently narrowing coverage.
